readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckLowerJetSmoothness.contDiffAt_lowerTerm
readback.mathematical_statement: E is the fixed real three-dimensional Euclidean space ClosedSmoothModel 3. Bilin is E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R, the normed space of continuous real bilinear forms represented as continuous linear maps from E to its continuous real dual. Jet1 is E ->L[R] Bilin, so its arguments consist of one derivative-direction slot followed by two bilinear-form slots. The declaration has no universe parameters. Before its mathematical quantifiers, the revised literal type locally selects the standard Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedAddCommGroup and ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedSpace instances for Jet1, explicitly fixing both scalars to R, source E, target Bilin, the identity real ring homomorphism, and the real scalar action. These are the canonical continuous-linear-map structures: the Jet1 norm is its existing CLM operator norm and the scalar action is the existing pointwise real action. The local instance selections add no hypothesis or replacement norm, do not choose a new metric or topology, and retain the usual normed product Bilin times Jet1. Let B be any fixed continuous real bilinear E-valued map E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E, and DB any fixed continuous real trilinear E-valued map E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E. Let G0 be any Bilin and J0 any Jet1. Assume only G0.IsInvertible, which means that the continuous real-linear map G0 : E ->L[R] (E ->L[R] R) is the forward map of a continuous linear equivalence E -> E dual. This is not an entrywise reciprocal, scalar inverse, or positive-definiteness premise. No symmetry of G0 or J0 is assumed; G0 need not be a positive Riemannian metric, J0 need not be a realized spatial derivative, and DB need not be the derivative of a background field whose value is B. Then the actual Bilin-valued function (G,J) |-> DeTurckPrincipalIdentity.lowerTerm B DB G J is C-infinity at the point (G0,J0) in the normed product space. The regularity is ContDiffAt R at the ENat top injected into WithTop ENat, rather than the outer top regularity value. B and DB are fixed throughout this metric-value/first-jet variation; the assertion is not joint smoothness in B,DB,G,J. The pinned lowerTerm is exactly (-2) smul ricciFirstBilin G J + J(fieldValue G J B) + G.comp(fieldFirstOperator G J B DB) + (G.flip.comp(fieldFirstOperator G J B DB)).flip. Evaluated in vector slots v,w, it is -2 * ricciFirst G J v w + J(fieldValue G J B) v w + G(fieldFirst G J B DB v) w + G v (fieldFirst G J B DB w). The fieldValue, fieldFirst, and ricciFirst are the existing finite-basis contractions built from G, J, fixed B/DB, and the actual connection G J u v = G.inverse(koszul J v u), retaining this Koszul argument order. The Koszul covector satisfies koszul J u v q = (1/2) * (J u v q + J v u q - J q u v). The inverse in these formulas is ContinuousLinearMap.inverse: at invertible G it is the continuous linear inverse from E dual to E, and the total definition returns the zero map when G is not invertible. The smoothness conclusion concerns the whole continuous-bilinear-map-valued lowerTerm in its existing operator-norm topology, not merely separate scalar evaluations at fixed v,w or an existential lower-order witness. It is local at invertible G0 and does not claim global smoothness across singular bilinear forms. No manifold, chart, cutoff germ, time interval, Hoelder exponent, second metric jet, curvature, flow, coefficient bound, or assumed linear operator package occurs in this type. The theorem does not state an explicit Frechet derivative or full finite-jet DQ formula, spatial coefficient regularity, covariance, a bounded global L, or a signed global residual/contraction. In particular it supplies no differentiation identity for the principal second-jet coefficient and cannot itself remove the later Da(G0)[h] applied to H0 contribution.
